newsitem.title: USA: Poll suggests apathy over White House invitations.
newsitem.headline: Poll suggests apathy over White House invitations.

text.p: The public is showing few signs of outrage over President Bill Clinton's invitations to let Democratic Party campaign contributors stay overnight in the Lincoln bedroom in the White House, according to a CNN/USA Today/Gallup Poll released on Thursday.
The poll said 63 percent said it was "typical" of the use of the White House by presidents of both parties to raise campaign funds, while 22 percent said it was worse.

Asked how they felt about Clinton's role in fund-raising, 45 percent said they did not care one way or another, 27 percent said they were disappointed but not angry, 13 percent said they were angry and 11 percent said they were pleased.
The poll said 42 percent believed it was all right to invite donors to stay there, and an equal proportion said it was wrong.
Fifty-three percent said the fuss over the issue was irrelevant to Clinton's character or his ability to do his job while 39 percent said it was relevant.
Half of those polled opposed naming an independent counsel to investigate the fund-raising affair, while 43 percent said a special prosecutor should be named.

Clinton has denied doing anything wrong in inviting friends and donors to the White House which has caused a major furore over the propriety of using the White House to reward large contributors to the Democratic Party.
The nationwide poll of 627 adults was taken Wednesday and had a margin of error of plus or minus four percentage points.
